To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nonpertubative effects on the fermions propagator are very significant when one studies the spin susceptibility corresponding to an antiferromagnetic staggered spin correlation.

the staggered spin correlations in the framework of Dyson-Schwingers approach are studied in detail, and that the nonpertubative dressing effects of the fermion self-energy on the staggered spin susceptibilities are very important in both the Nambi and Wigner phases.

the staggered spin response in QCD is dominated by the nonperturbatively dressed propagators and vertices, and that the spin correlation length in the Wigner phase is significantly larger than that in the Nambu one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the staggered correlation in the framework Dyson-Schwering approach, in which the full vertex function is included.
the study of the staggered magnetization and the staggered spin correlations in the framework of QCD.
the staggered spin correlations in the framework of Dyson-Schwingers approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nonpertubative effects of the full vertex functions are crucial in order to understand the staggered spin correlations in both the N ambu phase and the Wigner phase.
the staggered spin correlations in QCD are not strong enough to induce the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio type phase transition in the chiral limit.
the staggered spin correlations are very important in both the N and the W phases, and they are also important in determining the critical temperature of the chiral phase transition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the staggered correlation in the Nambu-Jona Lasinio model, the nonperturbatively dressed fermion propagators are very important.
the nonperturbation dressing effects on the pseudoscalar vertex functions are also important in the calculation of the staggered susceptibility in the framework of Dyson-Schwingers approach.
the Dyson-Schinger approach provides a useful tool for studying the staggered spin correlations in the QCD phase diagram.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the staggered spin susceptibilities are much larger in the Wigner phase than in the Nambu-phase.
the staggered spin response function is a very useful quantity to probe the nontrivial properties of QCD in the low-energy regime.
, when the nonperturbatively dressed fermion propagator is used in the calculation of the staggered-spin susceptibility, the antiferromagnetism is enhanced.
